quiz.q: Why is the list wrapped in `Arc<Mutex<…>>`?
options: Many requests share it (Arc) and only one changes it at a time (Mutex)
Axum requires Vec to be wrapped
quiz.explain: Arc shares ownership across tasks; Mutex stops two writers colliding.

quiz.q: What happens to the books when you restart the server?
options: They're gone — they lived only in memory
quiz.explain: State is ordinary memory. Keeping data across restarts is the database's job (Part A3).

quiz.q: How does a handler get the state?
quiz.explain: The State extractor hands each handler a clone of what you passed to `.with_state`.

options: Axum hands every request its own copy (a cheap Arc clone)
quiz.explain: Each handler call gets a clone; cloning an Arc copies a pointer, not the data.

flashcards.back: Arc: many owners. Mutex: one at a time may change it.
